content.text: The warranty package here meets or exceeds our preferred position, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies the preferred position on every element. Vendor warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards (19.1) and material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications (19.1, 19.2). The conformance period is 90 days from the later of delivery or acceptance for Deliverables, and — because "Services" is defined to include the hosted software — conformance runs for the entire subscription term for Hosted Services, which meets or exceeds the 12-month software benchmark. Section 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law, a no-malicious-code warranty and a no-functionality-degradation commitment. Section 19.4 supplies the full remedy ladder (re-perform, repair or replace at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees) and expressly states the remedy is non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. Critically, the disclaimer in 19.5 does not swallow the express warranties: it is limited to implied warranties and states that no disclaimer limits any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy. Section 21.4 confirms caps survive failure of an exclusive remedy but does not convert 19.4 into a sole remedy or otherwise cut back the warranty. Acceptance in Section 6 reinforces rather than limits the warranty trigger (silence and payment are not acceptance, and rejection yields correction cycles plus refund). The only minor narrowing is that the malicious-code warranty covers code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," which is customary and not material enough to warrant a redline given the strength of the remainder.
